result:
I bumped the vulnerable gems in `Gemfile.lock`, but I haven't run the test suite. The only check was `bundle check`, which says the dependencies are satisfied. I also don't have the actual Dependabot alert list, so I picked the gems to update myself.

I ran `bundle update --conservative` on the gems that usually get advisories. Rails itself stayed at 7.0.8. These are the changes:

| Gem | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `nokogiri` | 1.15.4 | 1.19.7 |
| `loofah` | 2.21.4 | 2.25.3 |
| `rails-html-sanitizer` | 1.6.0 | 1.7.2 |
| `rack` | 2.2.8 | 2.2.26 |
| `rexml` | 3.2.6 | 3.4.4 |
| `rubyzip` | 2.3.2 | 2.4.1 |
| `net-imap` | 0.4.4 | 0.6.8 |
| `puma` | 6.4.0 | 8.1.2 |

- **Puma:** this is a major version jump (6 to 8), so it carries the most risk. Check that your server config still works with it.
- **Windows platform:** the lockfile no longer lists the `x86-mingw32` build of `nokogiri`, so a 32-bit Windows install would no longer resolve.

Compare the gem list against the open Dependabot alerts to confirm nothing is missing.
